belief: Things will never get better in this country.
origins: Every generation has seen decline, and today’s news cycle makes the problems seem endless. After disappointment with leaders and policies, hopelessness sets in, and we withdraw or grow bitter.
teaches: Jeremiah told exiles, “Seek the prosperity of the city to which I have sent you as exiles. Pray to the LORD on its behalf.” Solomon cautioned that it is unwise to ask why the old days were better than these (Ecclesiastes 7:10). Paul urged “petitions, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgiving be offered for everyone—for kings and all those in authority.” “Our citizenship is in heaven.” Nations rise and fall, but God’s purposes stand. Hope does not depend on any government, and neither does our calling to do good.
self_statements: The best days are behind us.
I want to give up on it.
errors: Believing the country is either great or doomed.
Feeling discouraged and concluding that nothing will change.
questions: What good is happening that the news does not cover?
What has improved in history that people once thought impossible?
What does Scripture say to people in hard places?
What can I do locally that makes a difference?
Where is my deepest hope placed?
truth: My hope rests in God, not in any government. I can pray for my nation, seek its good where I live, and do what I can. Citizenship in heaven frees me to serve here without despair.
hw_truths: I can seek the good of my city.
I can pray for those in authority.
log: Each week, note one good thing you did or noticed locally.
actions: Choose a set time and stop.
Serve a neighbor or a cause.
prayer: Lord, I am discouraged about our country. Anchor my hope in You, teach me to seek the good of my city, and use me where I am. Amen.
name_example: Sarah can write: “I will seek the good of my city and pray for it.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “Things will never get better in this country.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
